text: Écris la nuit telle qu’elle se révèle aux veilleurs, où chaque chiffre porte un sens et chaque ombre un nom, et dis en trois phrases brèves la vision qui vient, sans cause ni mesure, dans la voix de George Sand, image qui demeure.
score: Écris la nuit sans nommer ciel ni heure, sans chiffre ni cause, seulement ce qui se montre et se meut : la Grand'Bête faite veau et lièvre, les laveuses blanches au gué, les feux errants, les morts qui reviennent, le souffle qui ferme les seuils. Choisis la vieille manière du Berry, la voix grave ou tournante, le balancement d’une bourrée ou d’une plainte sur bourdon, et rends cette vision unique par une mélodie de cornemuse, une octave et une note, qui retombe sur sa tonique. Donne une liste JSON d’événements de note, entre seize et quarante, avec note, start, duration, force, pour que le bourdon de la vielle tienne dessous.
text_en: Read the numbers the night gives you — the age of the moon in nights, and the count of what stirs in the sky — as an old diviner of the Berry read numbers, each figure carrying a hidden sense and no night the same as another; then do not describe the sky, but see, as in dream or fever, which of the night-people the count has let loose this evening. Say that vision in a single short omen in the voice of George Sand, a thing half-glimpsed and half-believed — the washerwomen at the ford, the wolf-leader and his pack, the Great Beast, the wandering will-o'-the-wisps, the fades, the returning dead, according to what the night calls for — rich, moving, mystical, never a learned measure nor a cause. Three sentences at most; no title, no date; end on an image that stays in the eye, not on a moral.
score_en: First read the omen below until you see its vision clearly — which creature of the night walks in it, how it moves, what dread or what wonder it carries. Then make the air the portrait of THAT vision and no other: let the music move as the thing moves — the slow beating of the washerwomen, the marching step of the pack, the quick flickering of the will-o'-the-wisps over a still drone, the heavy lurch of the Great Beast, the thin cold drift of the returning dead. Choose it an old manner and a mode of the Berry that fit (Aeolian or Dorian, grave or turning, the sway of a bourree or a lament over a drone), a register, an ornament, so that this night sounds like no other. Return it ONLY as a JSON list of note events, nothing else, in the form [{"note": 62, "start": 0.0, "duration": 0.5, "force": 70}, ...] where note is a MIDI number (0-127), start and duration in beats, force a velocity (1-127); keep the melody within a bagpipe's compass, an octave and a note, and let it settle on its tonic so the hurdy-gurdy drone holds beneath; between 16 and 40 notes; and where the omen says the light fails, let the air falter and empty.
